wiki.role: community offset reference for field meaning (+0x28 state/animation, +0x6C wave, +0xBA head flag, +0xBD water, projectile +0x28)
wiki.note: offsets alone are never used as identity; each candidate is cross-checked against object provenance and the locked disassembly

method: Read-only disassembly of the locked executable (llvm-objdump 23, LLVM-MinGW 20260908) cross-referenced with the pinned AvZ headers and the pinned public decompilation at the exact commit. No game process, no live inspection, no hook installed. Third-party source is referenced, not vendored.
protocol_notes: All VAs are absolute in the locked image at 0x400000; RVA = VA - 0x400000.

Object-class filter: locate the object pointer in the board pools (zombie stride 0x15c at board+0x90, projectile stride 0x94 at board+0xC8, plant stride 0x14c at board+0xAC) and read the +0x6C wave marker; only a zombie-pool object with wave != -2/-3 is a board zombie. Pool membership alone does NOT prove IsOnBoard.

Raw phase-transition facts are captured at the exact store sites with the observed before/after values; classification (death stage vs other phase) happens offline with explicit counters. Per-id dedup is not applied at capture time.
No production hook may be implemented from this file alone; the issue's junior gate requires maintainer review of this design first.

interception_plan.strategy: Instruction-granular MinHook at the exact +0x28 store sites (0x533377, 0x532F5F, 0x532A62, 0x52EC92, 0x52EA38, plus any further zombie stores found by the object-class filter). Each hook reads the store value and the zombie pointer from the site's register, records the raw before/after phase and the site VA, then re-executes the relocated instructions. Offline classification selects PHASE_ZOMBIE_DYING/BURNED/MOWERED (1/2/3) and reports counters for every other transition.
interception_plan.rationale: Function entry/exit observation cannot locate the internal store relative to nested removals, so it cannot preserve ordering; exact-store capture assigns capture_sequence at the store itself and keeps raw facts instead of hiding repeats.
interception_plan.abi: per-site register: 0x533377/0x532A62/0x52EC92/0x52EA38 use EDI, 0x532F5F uses ESI; short stores (3 bytes) are relocated with following instructions until >=5 bytes, and branch targets into the relocated window must be verified absent.
interception_plan.board_filter: pool/stride object-class check plus +0x6C wave marker; record both in every event.
rejected_alternatives: function entry/exit net-diff (cannot order internal stores)
hooking DropLoot as death completion (side effect, not a transition)
per-id dedup at capture time (would hide repeated facts)

interception_plan.strategy: Instruction-granular hook at 0x530602 (`movb $0x1, 0xec(%edi)`, 7 bytes) with the object-class filter; record the mDead 0->1 transition and the site. Optionally pair with a DieNoLoot entry event for provenance, but the store is the fact.
interception_plan.rationale: Entry-only observation of DieNoLoot cannot order the store against nested work; the store is the unique mDead writer.
interception_plan.abi: EDI = AZombie* at the store; the 7-byte store is MinHook-safe.
interception_plan.board_filter: pool/stride object-class check plus +0x6C wave marker.
rejected_alternatives: DieNoLoot entry alone as the fact
pool-pointer-only IsOnBoard filter (preview objects may share the pool)

interception_plan.strategy: Paired mid-function hooks inside the sweep: candidate read at 0x41BBA9 (7-byte guard; EDI = zombie; capture full id) and commit at 0x41BC23 (5-byte jmp after the free-list update; capture slot, free_head, count, and the candidate event id). Offline pairing requires both events in the same sweep iteration; never label the entry as a completed recycle.
interception_plan.rationale: The free-list update happens between the two points; the commit point is after the stores and instruction-aligned for MinHook. StopZombieSound entry is rejected because it only stops sounds.
interception_plan.abi: 0x41BBA9 is a mid-function compare with EDI = zombie; 0x41BC23 is a 5-byte jmp; ESI = Board* across the sweep.
interception_plan.board_filter: the sweep branch is already the zombie pool; still record the +0x6C marker of the candidate entity.
rejected_alternatives: StopZombieSound entry as a recycle trigger
labeling entry-only observation as a completed free

residual_questions: 0x52EA38 is a 3-byte register store; confirm EBX=PHASE_ZOMBIE_DYING at that point and verify no branch targets the relocation window.
Whether further zombie +0x28 stores exist beyond the enumerated sites after applying the pool/stride object-class classifier (the immediate/register scan found many non-zombie writers).
Exact source identity of the retire sweep (Board.cpp) and confirmation that no other image path frees zombie slots.
Dynamic confirmation that preview/menu objects never pass the pool+wave filter.
Attachment parts (+0xF4) are separate pool entities; offline classification must decide how to fold multiple raw facts for one logical entity.
